title: WorkerManifest
description: Standard descriptor for an Orbital worker. Any scheduler implementation — including ones that do not use @orbital-stellar/worker-core — may emit a worker.manifest.json that conforms to this schema. Consumers (the Orbital verification engine, dashboards, scoring systems) can process manifests from any conformant emitter without operator cooperation.

manifestVersion.description: Version of this manifest schema the document conforms to. Currently must be "1.0.0". Minor bumps add optional fields; patch bumps are editorial. A major bump introduces a breaking change and changes the $id.

id.description: Stable, globally unique identifier for this worker definition. Recommended format: "<org>/<worker-name>", e.g. "my-org/xlm-price-oracle". This value appears in fire events and reputation records — changing it is a breaking change.

name.description: Short human-readable display name for this worker.

description.description: Optional free-text description of what this worker does.

version.description: Semantic version of this worker implementation. Consumers should treat a version change as a signal to re-evaluate the manifest.

trigger.description: What causes this worker to fire.

target.description: The Soroban contract and function this worker invokes when it fires.

latencyBound.description: The worker's contractual latency commitment. Used by the verification engine (19.1) to score workers: a fire that lands outside the bound is late regardless of network conditions. Without this field 'late' has no contractual meaning.

fireEvent.description: The Soroban event the target contract emits to confirm that the worker's invocation succeeded. The verification engine uses this event — fetched from Stellar RPC — to score a worker from its manifest alone, with no operator cooperation.

network.description: The Stellar network this worker runs on.

author.description: Operator identity, e.g. a GitHub handle or organisation name.

repository.description: URL of the source repository for this worker implementation.

tags.description: Optional freeform tags for discovery and filtering.

TriggerSpec.description: What causes a worker to fire. Currently only time-based (cron) triggers are defined; additional trigger classes will be added in later milestones without breaking the schema.

CronTrigger.description: A time-based trigger driven by a cron schedule. The worker fires once per matching window.

class.description: Identifies this as a cron (time-based) trigger.

cron.description: Standard five-field cron expression (minute hour dom month dow). E.g. "0 * * * *" for every hour.

timezone.description: IANA timezone name for evaluating the cron expression (e.g. "UTC", "America/New_York"). Defaults to UTC at evaluation time if absent, but explicit declaration is strongly recommended.

windowSec.description: Width of the fire window in seconds. The scheduler must fire within this window starting at the cron moment. Defaults to 60 if absent.

TargetSpec.description: The Soroban contract and function the worker calls when it fires.

function.description: Name of the Soroban function to invoke.

params.description: Optional ordered list of static parameter descriptors passed to the function. Dynamic parameters resolved at fire time are not described here.

ParamSpec.description: Describes one static parameter passed to the target function.

LatencyBound.description: The worker's contractual latency commitment. Defines what 'on time' means for scoring. A worker is late if its confirmed fire event lands outside the defined window after the trigger moment. This field makes W3 tier pricing expressible: tiers are latency SLAs, not subjective ratings.

maxSeconds.description: Maximum elapsed seconds from the trigger moment to the on-chain confirmation of the fire event. A worker is scored 'late' by the verification engine if the confirmed ledger timestamp exceeds triggerTime + maxSeconds.

targetSeconds.description: Optional target latency the operator aims to achieve in normal conditions. Used for P50/P99 dashboards. Must be less than maxSeconds.

tier.description: Optional human-readable tier label (e.g. "standard", "fast", "realtime"). Purely advisory — scoring uses maxSeconds, not this label.

FireEventSpec.description: Describes the on-chain Soroban event emitted by the target contract when the worker's invocation succeeds. The verification engine fetches this event from Stellar RPC and uses it to confirm execution — with no operator cooperation required.

contractId.description: Bech32-encoded address of the contract that emits the confirmation event. Usually the same as target.contractId but may differ for proxy patterns.

topics.description: Ordered topic matchers. The verification engine matches incoming events against these in order. At minimum one topic must be provided.

dataFields.description: Optional list of data field descriptors the engine may extract from the event payload for scoring metadata.

TopicMatcher.description: A single topic constraint used when matching a fire event.

LiteralTopicMatcher.description: Matches a topic that must be a specific symbol value (the most common first-topic pattern).

value.description: The exact Symbol string this topic must equal.

TypedTopicMatcher.description: Matches any topic of the given Soroban type (wildcard by type).

type.description: Soroban scalar type name the topic must match (e.g. "address", "u64").

DataFieldSpec.description: Describes one field in the fire event's data payload that the verification engine may extract.
